mis_merges.label: midterm election seasonality
subjects: Senate/House race shift and its read-through to Fed governor appointments
mis_merges.why: The Democrat Senate-race comeback tied to Fed-appointment risk is a distinct, timely political story an editor could lead with, but it is easy to miss buried under a seasonality-stats label.

mis_merges.label: ai narrative
subjects: Meta/Google routine AI product and infrastructure news
Anthropic researcher's viral AI-safety resignation warning
mis_merges.why: A viral warning that AI poses existential risk is provocative enough to be its own lead theme but is buried alongside routine product-launch and capex items under one label.

mis_merges.label: energy supply risk
subjects: Iran/Gulf oil-tanker conflict pushing Brent above $100
Russia-Ukraine drone strikes on gas infrastructure pushing European gas to a 2022 high
mis_merges.why: Oil and European gas are separate wars, commodities and regions; scanning this label for the oil story could cause an editor to miss the distinct Ukraine gas-strike story entirely.

mis_merges.label: european equity buy ideas
mis_merges.why: Greek banks and Inditex are minor single-name calls that would not have been standalone lead themes regardless of grouping; the theme-relevant Germany portion is already captured as fragmented.

mis_merges.label: us debt deficits
mis_merges.why: Both are deficit-adjacent and would likely land in the same fiscal brief; the dedollarization portion is already captured as fragmented with usd de risking risk.

notes: Fragmentation is dominated by two mega-clusters (oil/Middle East supply shock across six labels, vol/correlation compression across four) that alone push the share past threshold; three mis-merges bundle politically or thematically distinct stories that could plausibly change lead-theme selection.
